A0226.title: Multi-Modal Perception Cross-Validation
A0226.definition: Fusing and cross-validating outputs of heterogeneous sensors (LiDAR, camera, IMU, mmWave radar, ultrasonic) to downweight or alert when a single sensor's data is inconsistent with the rest, resisting single-point perception spoofing.
A0226.description: Multimodal perception cross-validation fuses heterogeneous outputs from LiDAR, cameras, IMU, millimeter-wave radar, and ultrasonic sensors to perform consistency checks. When a single sensor's data deviates from the consensus of other channels, its weight is reduced or an alert is triggered, thereby defending against single-point perception spoofing. The approach is based on the premise that 'it is difficult for a single-sensor spoofing attack to consistently deceive all channels simultaneously.' At the sensor fusion layer, each channel is scored for consistency. For example, if GNSS indicates displacement but the IMU detects no acceleration, or a LiDAR point cloud shows an obstacle while the camera's field of view contains no corresponding object, or ultrasonic and infrared ranging measurements contradict each other, the deviating channel is down-weighted or discarded. Trust-aware sensor fusion dynamically assigns weights to each channel, maintaining overall perception reliability even under single-point spoofing. This mechanism is a core defense for the perception layer of autonomous driving and mobile robotics, directly countering single-sensor attacks such as LiDAR point cloud injection, IMU acoustic interference, and GPS spoofing. When combined with A0014 (tamper-proof mechanisms) and A0178 (AIoT model security protection), the former ensures data integrity, while this approach detects anomalies through redundancy when data has already been contaminated.
A0226.limitation: Advanced attackers can compromise multiple channels to create pseudo-consistent data, or use slow drift to keep deviations within tolerance and bypass cross-validation. Sensor noise, clock skew, and legitimate environmental changes may also cause false positives. Fusion adds compute and latency overhead, while cost and power constraints limit full redundancy.
